title: SDK v1→v2 patterns: retries, streaming ergonomics, and migration examples playbook
creator: Aria Patel
description: Create a practical, language-agnostic playbook that documents patterns and runnable examples for migrating from SDK v1 -> v2. Scope includes: retry semantics (idempotency, dedup keys, backoff defaults), streaming ergonomics (client-side iterators, backpressure API, reconnect semantics), migration recipes for Python, TypeScript, and Go, and an automated changelog generation workflow that extracts deprecations and breaking changes from PR metadata.
changes_summary: Collates recommended code patterns and small helper shims to smooth common migration pain points: 1) how to translate v1 retry wrappers to the new v2 RetryPolicy object; 2) streaming consumer patterns: AsyncIterator -> stream.Readable wrappers and idiomatic Go channel adapters; 3) recommended metadata headers for idempotency/deduplication and timing out long-running streams; 4) changelog automation via a GitHub Action that parses PR labels and 'BREAKING:' footers.
acceptance_criteria: Playbook page published under docs/sdk/migration/v1-to-v2 with language tabs for Python/TS/Go
At least three runnable examples (one per language) in the migration-examples repo and linked from the playbook
Changelog automation job created that produces a draft release notes file on each milestone with categorized sections: Breaking, Deprecations, New features, Bug fixes
Internal review by Documentation and DX teams completed with sign-off
Two codemod snippets (Python and TS) demonstrating automated rename patterns and streaming API shape changes
migration_steps: Audit existing v1 usages in the monorepo (search for .retry, stream.consume, and deprecated helper imports)
Map out common retry callsites and mark idempotent vs non-idempotent interactions
Add transient compatibility shims in 'sdk-compat' package to accept v1 args and translate to v2 types for a 3-month deprecation window
Publish playbook and examples; include a checklist for SRE teams to validate latency and error-rate after migration
Enable changelog GitHub Action on the SDK repo to collect PR metadata and push a release-draft to the milestone

examples: Python: how to replace response.stream_chunks() with client.stream.subscribe() and use async for with graceful reconnect
TypeScript: upgrading from EventEmitter-based streaming to AsyncIterable with automatic backpressure handling and a small wrapper for Node streams
Go: converting callback-based streaming handlers to ctx-aware channel adapters and recommended pattern for closing KV caches on cancellation
codemods_and_tools: python-codemod: rename 'sdk.retry' -> 'sdk.retry_policy' and convert dict args to RetryPolicy constructor calls
ts-codemod: replace .on('data') handlers with for-await-of AsyncIterable adapters; helper: scripts/ts/stream-adapter.ts
lint-rule: eslint rule to detect deprecated v1 imports and suggest quick-fixes
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Automatic retry changes could double-submit non-idempotent requests. Mitigation: default conservative retry counts and require explicit opt-in for retry on non-idempotent ops; add integration test harness that simulates duplicate side-effects.
Risk: Streaming consumers may fail silently under reconnection; Mitigation: provide clear reconnection semantics in playbook and sample harness that asserts delivery guarantees are preserved.
Risk: Changelog automation mis-classifies PRs. Mitigation: add a validation step in the Action that flags PRs missing required labels and comments reviewers when classification cannot be determined.
